## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `state-erased-signal-recovery`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-31T14:19:33.829Z.

Catalog entry, by slug: state-erased-signal-recovery

Recorded 2026-07-31. Extends the catalog; no prior entry is renumbered or restated. Owner recorded on the algorithm portfolio registry. Distinct from co-mutation-cohort-inference recorded earlier today: that entry infers ordering that was never authored, from the timing of co-mutation; this entry recovers ordering that WAS authored and that the lifecycle deleted. The two are complementary and their precision differs by construction - an inference versus a recorded claim.

The corpus shape this exists for. Every assembler in this catalog scores candidates against current item state. Measured on this tracker today, current item state is a lossy projection of the record, and it is lossy in exactly the dimension the assemblers most need. clearClosedBlockerSignals in the close path removes every blocked_by dependency row when an item closes, unconditionally. The consequence in the corpus: of 1,900 closed items exactly ONE retains a recorded predecessor, while the reverse spelling blocks, which no lifecycle path touches, survives on 189. The immutable stream still holds all of it - the close history entry lists dependencies among its changed_fields, and a point-in-time read reconstructs the deleted row - so the ordering facts exist, are hash-chained, and are simply not in the projection anyone queries.

The general principle, stated once so it outlives this particular defect. Item state is the current value of a fold over the stream, and the fold is not information-preserving: close deletes ordering edges, redaction marks values, compaction prunes checkpointed prefixes, and any future lifecycle rule may delete more. Therefore any relevance signal that the lifecycle can erase must be computed from the stream and not from the fold. This is not a workaround for one bug. It is a statement about which of the two representations is authoritative for scoring, and the answer is the one that is append-only.

The algorithm. Let S be an item's history stream, an ordered sequence of entries each carrying a timestamp, an author identity, an operation, a JSON patch, and before/after hashes. Define the edge-lifetime relation: for each patch operation that adds a dependency row, emit (source, target, kind, added_at, added_by); for each patch operation that removes one, emit the matching removal with removed_at and the operation that removed it. Folding these pairs yields, for every edge the workspace has ever held, an interval of validity rather than a boolean of presence. An edge deleted by a close has a closed interval whose right endpoint is the close instant; an edge still present has a half-open interval.

Scoring reads intervals, not presence. A candidate's ordering position is computed over the union of currently-present edges and edges whose interval ended in a lifecycle transition rather than in an explicit authored removal - the distinction is available because the removing operation is recorded, so a close-time clear is separable from a user calling update to retract a claim they no longer believe. Retracted edges are excluded; lifecycle-erased edges are included and carry a provenance marker so a consumer can see that the ordering came from the stream rather than from state. Relevance for a candidate then uses ordering depth over this recovered digraph, which on this corpus moves the input from a frontier of 1,845 of 2,104 nodes to a digraph whose predecessor coverage is bounded below by the number of ordering edges ever authored rather than by the number that survived.

Complexity and why it is affordable at scale. The fold is linear in stream length and touches only entries whose patch mentions dependencies, which is a small fraction: on this tracker 44,408 entries across 2,244 streams, of which dependency-bearing entries are a low-thousands subset. Critically the fold is monotonic in stream length, because the stream is append-only, so the result is cacheable keyed by (stream id, entry count, tail hash) and an incremental update reads only entries appended since the cached point. This is the same content-addressed discipline the attested-reads work uses, and it composes with it: an assembly that recovered ordering from the stream can attest which entry ranges it read.

Small-project and large-project behaviour. On a workspace of a few items spanning minutes, the fold is a handful of entries and the recovered digraph equals the authored one, because nothing has closed yet - the algorithm degenerates gracefully to reading current state and costs nothing. On a workspace of millions of items spanning decades, the recovery is per-item and embarrassingly parallel, the cache key makes re-reads free, and the only global step is the union, which is a streaming merge. Compaction is the one interaction that needs care: a checkpointed and pruned prefix loses the patch detail this fold depends on, so the compaction path must either retain dependency-affecting patches or record the derived edge intervals into the checkpoint before pruning. That is a real constraint on the compaction design and should be stated there rather than discovered later.

The falsifiable claim, and how to test it without trusting this note. Recover intervals for the whole corpus and count predecessor coverage over the recovered digraph. If the deletion hypothesis is right, coverage rises by roughly the number of blocked_by rows ever added minus those explicitly retracted, and the recovered predecessors for closed items should reconcile against the 189 surviving blocks rows on the other endpoint - the same real prerequisites recorded from the opposite direction should appear in both populations. If recovered coverage barely moves, the deletion is not the dominant cause and the ordering deficit is genuinely an authoring gap after all, which would falsify both this entry and the finding it rests on. That reconciliation is the test worth running first, because it is cheap and it discriminates between the two competing explanations.

What this entry does not claim. It does not propose changing the close semantics; that is a product decision tracked separately. It also does not assert that a lifecycle-erased edge is still a live constraint - it is explicitly historical, and a scheduler must not treat a recovered edge as an unmet prerequisite. The recovery is for understanding what happened, which is what a context assembler needs, and not for deciding what is actionable, which is what readiness needs. Conflating those two is the mistake that made blocked_by carry both meanings in the first place.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
